server.description: The physical units, deterministic: a unit as written resolved to its quantity and its UCUM code, a value converted between units of one quantity, two units compared, and a source's value checked against a request's restatement of it in another unit; the tool to ask whenever a unit or a quantity is refused or unknown
server.instructions: Never convert a unit in your head: ask units_convert, and check what you copy from a document with units_validate_connection (the document's value and unit as the source, yours as the target). A unit the system does not know is refused, never guessed: write the quantity beside it. When a unit or a quantity is refused (UNKNOWN_UNIT, UNKNOWN_QUANTITY, a unit that is not one of the quantity's), ask here before writing it again: units_normalize with the unit alone says which quantity takes it, with a quantity it says that quantity's units. A word of a property's name is not its quantity (a speed in percent is not a Speed, a velocity).

units_normalize.title: Resolve a unit
units_normalize.description: A unit as written (m3/min, m³/min, L/min, ppm, kg/s...), with its quantity when known (VolumetricFlow, Concentration, MassFlow...): the quantity it belongs to, its UCUM code, its symbol and its factor to the quantity's base unit. Ambiguous without the quantity when the same code belongs to two quantities. The first thing to ask when a unit or a quantity is refused: the unit alone gives the quantity it belongs to.

units_convert.title: Convert a value
units_convert.description: A value converted from one unit to another of the same quantity, by the substrate's tables; refused across quantities (m3/min to kg/s is not a conversion). Its answer carries cite, the justification of the converted number (source derived, the conversion as the reference), to write as it is.

units_compatible.title: Compare two units
units_compatible.description: Whether two units measure the same quantity, and which quantities they measure when they do not.

units_validate_connection.title: Check a restated value
units_validate_connection.description: A source states a value in its unit (a datasheet: 1.0 m3/min); a request restates it in another (60 L/min). Converted, they must agree within the tolerance (2 percent by default): OK with the expected value, or INVALID_CONVERSION with what the restatement should have been.

units_relations.title: The relations between quantities
units_relations.description: The conversions between different quantities a physical relation ties together, read off the knowledge graph (units_knowledge), each with its formula, the law it follows, its parameters (their units, the defaults the library's facts give) and which side is a derived reading rather than a quantity of the unit system.

units_relate.title: Convert to a related quantity
units_relate.description: A value converted from one quantity to a related one (units_relations lists them), instead of redoing the physics: 0.69 g/min of CO2 as L/min, 1000 ppm as mg/m3, a scrubber's kg/s from a 30 m3 volume as ppm per minute. The answer names the formula and says which parameters were given and which took the cabin's default (101 325 Pa, 293.15 K, CO2's molar mass). Refused when no relation ties the two quantities, or a parameter without a default (a volume) is missing. Its answer carries cite, the justification of the number obtained (source derived, the formula with its values as the reference), to write as it is.

properties.value: the value, in the from unit
properties.from: its quantity and unit, e.g. {quantity: MassFlow, unit: g/min}
properties.to: the related quantity and the unit wanted, e.g. {quantity: VolumetricFlow, unit: L/min}
properties.parameters: by name, a number in the parameter's unit or {value, unit}: V (the volume, m3), P (Pa), T (K), M (kg/mol)

units_knowledge.title: The knowledge graph of the relations
units_knowledge.description: The graph the relations are read from, to navigate: with id, a node (a quantity, a unit, a constant, a law, a relation) and its typed links in and out (from, to, parameter, follows, uses, measures); with from and to, the shortest chain of relations from one quantity to the other; with type, the nodes of that type (physics.quantity, physics.relation, ...).

properties.id: a node's id, or a quantity's name
properties.type: a type of the ontology, to list its nodes
properties.from: a quantity, the start of a chain
properties.to: a quantity, the end of a chain
